principle_text: When the persuadee is sharing personal experiences and enthusiasm unrelated to the charity, avoid focusing solely on small talk without gradually steering the conversation toward the donation topic.

When the persuadee is engaged in casual, friendly conversation without indication of donation interest, avoid continuing only small talk that does not connect to the charitable cause or donation appeal.
When the persuadee shares personal interests or locations, avoid responding with only factual answers that do not connect to the charitable cause or advance the donation conversation.
When the persuadee is engaged in friendly, neutral conversation without donation-related cues, avoid making statements that do not connect to the charitable cause or donation appeal.
When the persuadee shows interest in casual conversation topics without indicating donation intent, avoid continuing only friendly exchanges that do not connect to the charitable cause.
When the persuadee expresses shared values and curiosity about giving back, you should highlight your own charitable actions to build rapport and open the door for donation discussions.

When the persuadee shows interest in volunteerism or charitable activities, you should introduce a reputable and personally meaningful organization to build connection and encourage positive engagement.
When the persuadee expresses financial constraints or unwillingness to donate immediately, avoid making direct requests for contributions that may pressure or alienate them.
When a persuadee politely declines to donate due to current financial constraints, avoid insisting that donating would not cost them anything as it may come across as dismissive and pushy.
